description:
The crate ships a flat set of free functions:

  pub fn from_pem(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>
  pub fn from_der(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<TrustAnchor, Error>
  pub fn from_der_iter<I, B>(iter: I) -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>
  pub fn from_pem_file(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>
  pub fn from_der_file(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<TrustAnchor, Error>

There is no `TrustStoreLoader` / `Loader` / `LoaderOptions` struct. There
is no builder. The free functions have no extensibility seam.

Future additions that already have placeholder beads or known need:

  - Strict NameConstraints loading (PKIX-tit4.1: use TrustAnchor::try_from
    instead of from_cert so malformed NC fails closed). A 'strict' mode
    flag would naturally live on a loader struct.
  - Per-anchor filter callback (Mozilla's 'serverAuth only' bit, root
    program ingestion rules — README explicitly lists per-anchor trust
    policy as an explicit non-goal for now, but the README says 'revisit
    when a concrete consumer asks for it'). When revisited, the API
    needs an extensibility seam.
  - Warning channel (PKIX-tit4.1 option c: 'surface a per-anchor warning'
    for soft failures). A `&mut Vec<Warning>` parameter or a configurable
    callback both want a loader-shaped home.
  - Caller-supplied 'now' for time-of-load validity-period filtering (a
    deployment may want to drop anchors that have already expired at
    load time rather than at validation time).
  - Memory-mapped or chunked loading for very large bundles (lib.rs:391
    already calls out 'tens of MB' as the rough threshold).

With the current API, each of these is either:

  a) A new function name (`from_pem_strict`, `from_pem_with_filter`,
     `from_pem_with_warnings`, …). The surface grows linearly with
     options and the combinations explode.
  b) An overloaded signature change. Each is a breaking change to the
     public function (pre-1.0 free; post-1.0 a major bump).

Both are worse than admitting a `LoaderOptions` struct now while there are
no consumers to migrate.

Pre-1.0 framing (from AGENTS.md 'Design for the eventual complete shape'):
this is exactly the moment to decide whether the eventual shape is
'function-per-source × option-permutation' or 'small loader struct + per-
source method.' The latter scales; the former does not.

Counter-argument: if 'no options will ever need to be added' is the
maintainer's call, the current shape is fine. The README's 'Per-anchor
trust policy is out of scope; revisit when a concrete consumer asks for
it' suggests options WILL be added eventually, which makes the current
shape a pre-1.0 forward-compat trap.

This is flagged 'opinion' because reasonable maintainers prefer free
functions for simple bytes-in/anchors-out plumbing. But the architectural
question deserves an explicit decision rather than 'we never thought to
ask.'
title: Free-function API forecloses on extensibility seams; future options must use new names
